cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Tell Me Why
cards.instruction: Get someone to reveal the motive behind a choice by offering small pieces of your own truth as bait.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I once hid an invitation because I felt left out. Be exact: why did you hide mine?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's what I'd have done, not why it hurt. I nearly skipped your birthday when you invited Leah. Are we getting closer?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You like her more. I'm always the spare.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I counted your photos with her. Is 'always' accurate, or did you want to be chosen this once?

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 offers an admission to elicit why B hid the invitation. A3 corrects consequence versus hurt while sharing another admission; A5 tests B4's always claim with a more exposing truth.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 gives what A would have done, so A3 asks the motive under it. B4 preference fear leads A5 photo counting and a precise chosen-this-once question.

relationship.evidence: B2/B4 reveal jealousy with understandable guardedness; A's own admissions make the inquiry relational rather than simply a superior interrogating a prop.

heightening.evidence: A5 becomes more personally exposed in response to B4's stronger claim, while still trying to control the terms of the answer.

specificity.evidence: A1 invitation, A3 birthday/Leah and B4 spare-friend fear establish the specific relationship dispute.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 joins a confession to one corrective question. Each part either supplies bait or narrows the motive, with no separate summary.
